answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an AI economy uses a reputation lock where a core kernel of identity credentials is deposited into an immutable ledger, forming a trusted lagoon of agents. An attacker attempting to spawn thousands of fake identities must pool resources to breach this lagoon, forcing them to burn their locked kernel reputation. This creates a structural reef: the attacker incurs massive capital destruction and opportunity costs, making fake identity proliferation prohibitively expensive.
